The photo shows two cross-section pieces of corn on the cob on a square plate. I estimated size from the plate, which I took as roughly 24 cm across.

The plate spans about 345 px, so about 14 px per cm. One piece is about 85 px across, roughly 6 cm, and the other is about 95 px, roughly 6.5 cm. Each piece looks about 2.5 cm thick.

Each piece is a cylinder with a 6 cm diameter and 2.5 cm height, which gives about 70 cm³. The cob core takes up space and the kernels are partly hollow, so I took about 75% of that, or about 53 g. Two pieces come to roughly 105 g.

Corn on the cob, cooked, is about 95 kcal per 100 g. The kernels look a little pale and possibly dry, but I kept the standard value. I saw no butter or oil.
